honest_verdict.what_this_run_actually_did: Hashed Moore Dkt 3188, Kirschner Dkt 3190, and Moore deck Dkt 3466. Extracted a Katsumi invoice-amount collision ($240.35 vs $434,997.58) that is not in Adv. 25-03803 Doc. 17 ¶ 54 / ¶¶ 72–74 or the public indictment example amounts. Examiner 2538-2 PDF still not retrieved.

best_cashe_shaped_finding.claim: On September 22, 2023 Katsumi asked First Brands for copies of seven invoices it had already funded. On September 25 a Romania AR analyst sent the invoices without routing them through Brumbergs or Edward James. None of the seven matched funded amounts. The extreme instance: an invoice actually worth $240.35 had been funded as $434,997.58 (more than 180,000% inflation). Katsumi escalated September 27-28 and then funded about $4.9 billion more.
best_cashe_shaped_finding.why_it_matters: Invoice-amount collision with two named dollar amounts, a dated audit path, and a named factor. Not the Doc. 17 ¶ 54 GM $179.84 / $9,271.25 example and not the public indictment June 2025 $8,976.24 / $17,826.26 / $463,734.92 example. No invoice number or customer name is given.

prior_best_cashe_shaped_finding.claim: On April 4, 2025, SPV Carnaby FA opened the day with $4,833.98, received $67.2 million from an Onset sale-leaseback, and the same day paid approximately $17 million to the Patrick James Trust.
prior_best_cashe_shaped_finding.why_it_matters: This is a falsifiable, three-node cash path (opening balance -> financing inflow -> insider outflow) on a single calendar day. The public indictment excerpts describe invoice fraud and enrichment generally; they do not recite this Carnaby FA day.

source.doc: First Brands v. James, Adv. Proc. No. 25-03803, Doc. 17 (filed Nov. 3, 2025) ¶ 72

strongest_candidate_pending_primary.claim: Aequum lent about $43.8 million to SPV Broad Street against Cardone inventory First Brands purported to sell. Debtors' May 4, 2026 amended answer (Adv. 26-03091 ECF 25) is reported to admit FBG did not have an interest in the goods it purported to sell. Jerneycic is reported to have found about $42.9 million routed through Bowery Finance II. Judge Lopez signed a PI on June 25, 2026 (ECF 140; amended ECF 174 on Aug 3) and is reported to have observed that substantially all proceeds went to Bowery, no funds reached Cardone, and the record lacked transfer documents — while not deciding ultimate ownership. Aequum later liquidated the inventory for about $20 million.
strongest_candidate_pending_primary.why_it_matters: Named asset (Cardone inventory) plus named cash path (Aequum -> Broad Street -> Bowery) plus a reported debtor admission of no title. Not in the public indictment or first-day declaration at this granularity.
